name: Multimodal Inputs
question: How should the agent read documents, images and screenshots?
summary: Multimodal models read images directly: scanned documents, phone photos, screenshots and charts. Quality depends on the input: deskewing, cropping and resizing to the model’s limits matter, and small text may need tiling or zoom. For fields that matter, such as KYC details or claim amounts, a second reader such as OCR or a second model cross-checks the first, and disagreements go to a person.

items.detail: too low loses text; tiles cost more
checksums and formats on extracted fields

Extract into a schema with per-field confidence

Validate formats and route disagreements to people
pitfalls: Sending huge images that the API downscales anyway

remember: Clean the image, read it twice, check the fields.
caption: Illustrative accuracy for printed and handwritten regional documents.

steps.title: Straighten and crop
steps.text: Phone photos are tilted and include the table they sit on. Deskewing and cropping to the document gives the model a clean page.

steps.title: Resize to the model’s limit
steps.text: Very large images are downscaled by the API anyway; resizing yourself keeps text as legible as possible within the limit.

steps.title: Read into a schema
steps.text: The vision model extracts named, typed fields, so its output can be validated rather than parsed from prose.

steps.title: Read it again, differently
steps.text: OCR independently reads the same image. Amounts, dates and names must appear in both readings.

steps.title: Disagreements go to a person
steps.text: When the two readers disagree, an assessor checks the document. Most errors are caught here.

steps.title: Accept the rest
steps.text: Documents where both agree go straight through. Wrong amounts reaching the claims system fell below 3%.

practice.scenario: A fictional general insurer receives claim documents as phone photos on WhatsApp: hospital bills, discharge summaries and pharmacy receipts, some handwritten in Hindi or Marathi. OCR followed by a text model misread 30% of handwritten fields. The new pipeline deskews and crops each photo, reads it with a vision model into a schema, cross-checks amounts and dates with OCR, and sends disagreements to an assessor. Wrong amounts reaching the claims system fell below 3%.

industries.use: Bills, receipts and discharge summaries from phone photos

practice.analogy: Two clerks read each important form independently, and a supervisor looks only where they disagree.

library.name: A vision model + OpenCV + Tesseract
library.what: Preprocess with OpenCV, extract with a vision model into a schema, and cross-check key fields with OCR.

practice.note: Match numbers after normalising digits and separators, including Devanagari digits. Keep the original image for the audit trail (Panel 15).

numericDrill.question: A pipeline reads 10,000 claim documents a month. The vision model is wrong on 4% of key fields, and cross-checking with OCR catches 70% of those errors and sends them for review. How many documents a month still reach the system with a wrong key field?
numericDrill.answer: 10,000 × 4% = 400 wrong; 70% caught leaves 400 × 0.3 = 120 documents. The cross-check also sends correct documents to review when the two readers disagree, so tune it to keep that load manageable.

interview.question: How would you read KYC documents with a multimodal model safely?
interview.answer: Preprocess images by deskewing, cropping and resizing; extract into a strict schema; validate formats and checksums; cross-check critical fields with a second reader such as OCR; route disagreements to a person; mask identifiers in logs; and keep the original image for audit.

interview.question: Why does image resolution matter for a vision model?
interview.answer: APIs downscale large images to a maximum size, so small text can become unreadable, and very low resolution loses detail. Resize deliberately to the model’s limit, crop to the document, and tile or zoom into regions with small text when needed, accepting the extra cost.

mistakes.mistake: Trusting a single read for amounts or IDs
